absent: Internals of slot lookup, follow, dirty marking, pinning, and host page lifetime beyond the call boundary.
Architecture virtual CPU hooks for create, run, state access, fault, and extension handling.
Complete generic extension list and default handling for unknown extensions beyond the truncated switch.
Dirty ring allocation, release, sizing, and page retrieval mechanics.
Virtual CPU initialization, load and put, reference counting, and statistics header contents.
Device operation creation, initialization, release, destroy, and full operations table contents.
Run structure size guarantees and input output remap attributes beyond success or failure.
Unmap, wake, scheduler, and signal interactions during kick and pre fault beyond what is shown.

findings.text: Guest frame numbers resolve to host addresses through the owning memory slot. The virtual machine wide helpers look up the slot for the machine and the virtual CPU scoped helper looks up the slot for the calling virtual CPU, then all delegate to a slot relative conversion. The protected variants also report writability through a caller supplied out parameter.

A helper translates a guest frame number to a refcounted host page. It builds a follow context carrying the resolved slot, the frame number, a write flag derived from the caller boolean, and a receiver for the page, invokes the generic follow routine, discards its numeric result, and returns the received page which may be absent when lookup fails.

A virtual CPU mapping operation pins and maps one guest frame for host access. It prepares a follow context from the virtual CPU slot with write intent and pin request, records frame and writability while clearing prior host state, follows to a host frame number, rejects a missing slot encoding with an invalid argument error, then establishes host access through a direct page mapping when valid and through an input output remap otherwise on capable builds, returning a fault error when no host address results.

The host mapping descriptor carries a pinned page pointer, a page pointer, a host address pointer, the guest frame number, a writability flag, and the resulting host frame number. Initialization clears the pointers before following and stores frame number and writability first, with the host address filled only after successful mapping.

Reusing a host mapping descriptor that already holds a host address triggers a one time warning check and releases the previous mapping before reinitializing. Callers must therefore release or expect implicit release before reuse rather than assuming idempotent overwrite.

Dirty tracking for a guest frame resolves the owning memory slot for the virtual machine and then records dirtiness within that slot. Slot lookup therefore precedes the per slot dirty update on every call.

A virtual CPU kick first attempts a lightweight wake and returns when it succeeds. When the target is the caller itself it moves guest mode to exiting guest mode without cross processor messaging. Otherwise after an architecture willingness check it reads the target processor, and only when that processor differs from the caller and is online and in range it sends either a blocking call or a reschedule signal depending on whether the caller waits.

The only mode change allowed outside the virtual CPU mutex is from in guest to exiting guest, which lets the same thread kick path avoid atomic operations. Migration may move the target after the willingness check and cause signaling to a prior processor, which remains correct because migration itself forces exit from guest mode.

Virtual CPU fault handling selects a backing page by fault offset. Offset zero maps the shared run structure, a platform input output offset maps architecture data, a coalesced input output offset maps the machine ring when enabled, and offsets inside the dirty ring window map the corresponding ring page, with all other offsets delegated to architecture fault handling. The chosen page is reference counted and returned with success.

The dirty ring occupies a contiguous page offset window starting at a fixed log offset with length derived from the machine dirty ring size divided by page size. On builds without ring support the membership predicate is always false.

Virtual CPU mapping validates dirty ring mappings and rejects executable mappings or non shared mappings that touch the ring window at either end. Otherwise it installs fault operations and succeeds without further checks.

Virtual CPU file operations expose release, unlocked control, mapping, no operation seek, and compat control behavior, while virtual memory operations expose only a fault handler. Release drops the machine reference held for the open file.

Each virtual CPU descriptor is an anonymous inode whose name encodes the numeric virtual CPU identifier and whose private data is the virtual CPU, using the virtual CPU file operations and opened read write with close on exec.

Virtual CPU process identifier reads hold a dedicated read lock while the run path updates the identifier under the write lock. The dedicated lock permits concurrent readers while the owning thread holds the virtual CPU mutex during execution.

Per virtual CPU debug support creates a directory named for the identifier under the machine debug directory and adds a read only process identifier file backed by an accessor, then invokes an architecture hook for additional entries. Creation is skipped when debug facilities are unavailable.

Virtual CPU creation validates the requested identifier against a maximum, rejects creation beyond the machine maximum and duplicate identifiers, and runs an architecture pre creation check before allocating. It allocates a zeroed virtual CPU object and a zeroed page for the run structure, initializes the virtual CPU, runs architecture creation, and optionally allocates a dirty ring when the machine has a ring size.

Creation progresses from validation through allocation, architecture creation, ring allocation, array insertion, descriptor creation, online publication, post creation and debug setup. Any failure unwinds the index to invalid, frees the ring, destroys architecture state, frees the run page and virtual CPU object, and decrements the created count, with array erasure and reference release on publication failures.

Creation holds the machine lock across validation and array insertion, then holds the virtual CPU mutex across descriptor creation and online count increment. The online increment follows a write barrier after storing the virtual CPU pointer, matching lookup ordering, and documents virtual CPU mutex nesting inside machine lock.
Setting a virtual CPU signal mask removes kill and stop from the supplied set, stores the result and marks it active, while a null input clears active state. The operation always reports success.

Virtual CPU statistics are exposed through a read only anonymous file whose name encodes the identifier. Reads delegate to a generic statistics helper with virtual CPU specific header, descriptors, counters and size, and release drops the machine reference acquired at creation. Descriptor allocation reserves a close on exec number before installing the file and releases it on file creation failure.

Pre faulting validates that flags are clear, address and size are page aligned, and the range does not wrap. It loads the virtual CPU and holds read protection while repeatedly invoking architecture pre fault, aborting on pending signals, zero or input output failure indications, or negative status, advancing the range by progress amount and yielding between iterations. It reports success when at least one page made progress even if a later iteration fails.

Pre faulting holds loaded state and source read protection across the whole range loop and releases both before returning. Waiting for online publication uses a fast online count check and otherwise acquires then releases the virtual CPU mutex in killable mode to block until creation publishes, returning interrupted on signal and input output error if the virtual CPU remains unreachable.

Virtual CPU control handling rejects calls from a foreign address space or dead machine, rejects non virtualization command types, waits for online publication, and offers architecture unlocked handling first. Only unclaimed commands take the virtual CPU mutex in killable mode and then dispatch to run, register, segment, multiprocessor, translation, debug, signal mask, floating point, statistics descriptor, and pre fault operations, with unknown commands delegated to architecture handling.

The run command requires a zero argument, refreshes the stored thread identifier when the calling thread changed after an architecture notification with reference exchange under write protection, sets a wants to run flag from the shared immediate exit request, invokes architecture run, clears the flag, performs an exit helper, and traces the exit reason with status.

Fixed size state controls allocate kernel buffers for gets and copy results to userspace, or copy from userspace for sets, delegating interpretation to architecture helpers and freeing temporary buffers on all exits. Signal mask input validates embedded length against host signal set size before copying the nested set, and pre fault copies back the leftover range.

Compat handling intercepts only signal mask with a compat length check and compat to native set conversion, delegating a null set to clear active state, and forwards all other commands to the native virtual CPU control path after the same address space and liveness checks.

Device file behavior delegates mapping, attribute access, and controls to per device operations. Attribute controls copy a descriptor from userspace and require the corresponding accessor, failing with permission when absent and fault on copy failure. Unknown controls use a custom device control when present and otherwise report inappropriate control. Mapping without device support reports no device.

Device release, when a release operation exists, holds the machine lock while removing the device from the machine list with read copy update semantics, synchronizing, and invoking release, then drops the machine reference in all cases. File to device conversion succeeds only when file operations match the device operations, otherwise returning null.

Device types index a fixed size operations table bounded by a maximum type constant. Only conditionally compiled entries are populated in the visible fragment and other slots are null and treated as missing devices.

Device creation bounds checks the requested type with speculation protection, rejects unknown types, and honors a test only flag with immediate success. Otherwise it allocates a device, stores operations and machine linkage, runs creation under the machine lock with list publication, runs optional initialization outside the lock, acquires a machine reference and anonymous descriptor, and on descriptor failure unwinds reference, list membership with synchronization, and release and destroy hooks.

Generic extension queries affirmatively report support for memory synchronization, user memory variants, region destruction and joining behavior, internal error data, any length event signaling, machine scoped extension and capability enablement, halt polling, and conditionally message interrupts, interrupt descriptors, and coalesced input output where configured.

The visible extension switch is truncated after the coalesced input output case, so the full set of generic extensions and the fallback for unknown extensions are not shown and must not be assumed from this lane alone.

Invoking virtual CPU controls before creation publishes risks null dereference through array lookup. The mitigation is an explicit online wait that serializes early callers on the virtual CPU mutex until the online count advances.
